notes.title: TBS: KT Art Focus 4
notes.content:
Greetings everyone!

If you have already played the first The Ballad Singer, you know that the three main pillars of the game are the visual arts, the music, and the fully narrated story.
Since The Ballad Singer: Knights Templar is an evolution of the first game, the focus will remain on those three aspects. This time we are going to have a managerial and combat phase that is going to make the game completely different. But the focus on visual art, music, and storytelling is still there.

The game includes a hard-core combat system, where 1 blow delivered by the opponent could be fatal if your unit does not wear armor.
Among the combat objectives, there is the "Massacre" where you have to slay most of the enemies.
Below you can find the image that we are using to show this objective!

-Riccardo

notes.title: TBS: KT Art Focus 3
notes.content:
Greetings everyone!

Today I am thrilled to share with you a handpicked selection of hit cards included in the weapons, as well as some of the unique perks of the unit or Grand Master.

In TBS:KT, each unit boasts a distinctive deck crafted around their equipment and perks. The combat phase sees you unleashing these unit cards, along with others from a special Command Deck featuring cards from archers and Grand Master perks.

It will be crucial to know that Command Deck cards are accessible to all units in combat, but require Faith Points to use, so you must make wise choices when playing them. At times, you will face tough decisions, such as deciding between rescuing your beloved unit or securing the battle's objective.

 -Riccardo

notes.title: TBS: KT Art Focus 2
notes.content:
Greetings everyone!

During the artistic realization, I divided all the cards into two categories: horizontal and vertical. The horizontal cards have a special role in the game as they are used for game activities and focus cards that can influence your gameplay with bonuses or maluses over a short period of turns.
The vertical ones are used for equipments, hits and more.

What's unique about the focus cards is that each one is named after a Latin proverb! We have provided translations for the proverbs and descriptions of the bonuses/maluses they offer. I believe this adds an extra layer of depth and medieval charm to the game.

Stay tuned for more updates on this exciting project!

 -Riccardo

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41956995/b4497f2f5e39cd10469e5f7fe7bc2f95d15c5aa6.png[/img]

notes.title: TBS: KT, Art Focus 1
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

I'm excited to introduce the "TBS KT: Art Focus" series with this post! Over the next few weeks, I'll be sharing some images that highlight the immense effort we've put into the game's graphics.

As with the first TBS game, we have three main strengths: illustrations, music, and story. The same artists from the first game have covered all three areas, ensuring continuity in this "second chapter" of the game. However, this time we're adding complexity to the game mechanics, so we're not relying entirely on the artists' features.

TBS KT is going to be completely different from the first TBS game, but the artistic focus remains the same. So, stay tuned for more posts in this series!

[b]TBS: KT, Art Focus 1[/b]

In TBS: KT, the [b]first phase[/b] of the fights take place in an isometric environment, and we've prepared modular pawns divided into the three factions of the game. The Templars are the playable faction, and one of the differences between the enemy factions is that they have cloth colors based on whether they are postulants, sergents, or knights.
The [b]second phase[/b] of the fights is using the decks build around the weapons and perks of the unit, and we will show it in the future.

Mounts like horses, camels, donkeys, and mixed breedings such as hinnies or mules also have different game stats, appearances and saddleclothes according to the faction. This modular system offers thousands of different combinations, allowing us to create each warrior as a unique unit with a dedicated portrait, name, background, trait, and ideal that differentiates them from other units.

Each unit also has a specific deck built around the perks and weapons you've chosen for them. This aspect is incredibly important to me, and I can't wait for you to see it in action.

-Riccardo

notes.title: Fight for your brothers!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41956995/9948db99477ca82fbc52abf50f29bbc87d8ef691.jpg[/img]

Cheers future Grand Masters, I want to share with you the current state of the game and the plans for the next year.
We are very close to having the first internal playable build of the game. This is a very critical step since we are going to try for the first time all the different parts of the game together.
The story will be linked to the managerial and combat phase and in the first months of next year, we will try to polish and balance how each activity interacts with the others.
Mounts and equipments are already part of the game as well as buildings and perks.

We are currently planning some insights on the game for next year.
[b]It could be interesting to know if you want to know more about some specific parts of the game, in this way we can deliver more interesting insights![/b]

Remember to follow us on Socials, we have already shared plenty of amazing story images of the game!

[url=https://www.facebook.com/CurtelGames]Facebook[/url]

[url=https://www.instagram.com/curtelgames/]Instagram[/url]
